requirements.text: A cumulative GPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — or a score percentile of 80% or above on a 100-point scale, or a rank in the top 20% of the class

The Embassy of Japan in Nepal requires 70% marks (CGPA 3.1) for Natural Sciences and 60% marks (CGPA 2.5) for Humanities and Social Sciences, averaged across the +2 and above degree. This is a Nepal-specific bar set by the mission, not a MEXT-wide rule.
requirements.scope_note: Nepal-specific. The mission sets this bar; MEXT's own guidelines do not. A reader applying from another country must check their own mission.

requirements.text: CGPA of at least B/B+ on the US system, or a 2nd upper classification on the UK system

3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent) is the minimum permitted GPA. KAUST adds context for applicants: typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3, and 75% have a GPA above 3.5 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent).
requirements.not_a_requirement: The figures 3.3 and 3.5 describe who was typically admitted, not a threshold. They are recorded here as context and must never be compared against.

of.quote: No minimum GPA is stated in the Edital.

requirements.text: No minimum GPA is stated in the Edital. Academic admission requirements are set by the individual postgraduate programme the candidate applies to, and the Edital states that CAPES's requirements and the programme's requirements are cumulative.

of.applies_to: top 10% of graduates in the previous study programme

requirements.text: Students must have achieved excellent academic results in their previous study programme(s), which must be relevant to the Master's programme for which they are applying. As an indication, the student is amongst the top 10% of graduates in his/her previous study programme. Note that proof of ranking is not required – this information is purely to indicate the level of competitiveness.
requirements.not_a_requirement: TU Delft states the 10% figure “as an indication” and says proof of ranking is not required. It is a statement of the competitive level, not a gate the reader is asked to evidence.

of.quote: There is no formula for admission, and there are no scores, achievements, or stories that automatically qualify you for admission.

requirements.text: Knight-Hennessy publishes two baseline eligibility requirements — admission to a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme, and a first bachelor's degree earned in January 2020 or later — and no academic threshold. The admission page states there is no formula for admission and no score that automatically qualifies an applicant.

of.varies_by: no published threshold — grades are one of four weighted criteria

requirements.text: KTH names four scholarship selection criteria, the first of which is “the applicant's grades (GPA or equivalent)”, alongside the ranking of the university that awarded the bachelor's degree, relevant extracurricular research or work experience, and the applicant's motivation on sustainable development. No minimum grade, GPA or class threshold is published.

of.varies_by: no published threshold — candidates are ranked against each other

requirements.text: Stipend-bearing Graduate Research Scholarships are “offered to eligibile candidates ranked highest by relevant selection panels based on their academic results for prior study and their research potential in their field of study”. No minimum GPA, WAM or honours class is published; the only stated eligibility is having applied for, or being enrolled in, a graduate research degree.

of.varies_by: the admitting university, not Chevening — no classification published by the scheme

requirements.not_a_requirement: A 2:1 (upper second-class) is widely repeated as a Chevening requirement in third-party guides. It does not appear in Chevening's own published eligibility criteria, which delegate the academic bar to the unconditional offer. It is recorded here as absent from the source, not as a threshold to meet.
requirements.text: Chevening's published eligibility requires an undergraduate degree “that qualifies you for a UK master's programme” and an unconditional offer from at least one of the three courses applied to. No degree classification, GPA or grade threshold is published by Chevening itself — the academic bar is set by the university making the offer, not by the scheme.

of.varies_by: the admitting university via University Admissions — SI assesses no academic criterion

requirements.text: SI publishes no academic threshold for the Scholarship for Global Professionals. The documents it requires are a CV, proof of work and leadership experience, two references, a passport copy and a motivation statement — no transcript or record of grades is requested. Admission, and with it the academic entry requirement, is handled by University Admissions rather than by SI.

Admission is subject to the approval of the TERRA Managing Board and is based on the applicant's academic ability, motivation, recommendation letters and language proficiency. Applications will be assessed solely on academic merit, ability and potential. The academic evaluation of the candidate's curriculum is based on the following criteria: previous higher education studies; content and relevance of prior studies / quality of the awarding institution; relevant professional experience; recommendation letters; motivation letter; additional information (publications, awards, etc.). No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class rank is published as a bar.

Applicants are expected to have a higher education degree with a minimum of: a Bachelor's degree with 240 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to 4 years of study), or Bachelor's and/or Master's degree(s) with 300 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to 5 years of study) — the 300-credit requirement is mandatory for all students whose mobility track includes UNIFI. Applicants must hold a degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture or equivalent qualifications.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNIFI, 240 ECTS otherwise

requirements.text: Admission to NORISK will be decided on a competitive basis; the students are assessed on the basis of their previous academic record. Applications will be assessed solely on academic merit, ability and potential. The academic evaluation of the candidate's curriculum is based on the following criteria: previous higher education studies; content and relevance of prior studies / quality of the awarding institution; relevant professional experience; recommendation letters; motivation letter; additional information (publications, awards, etc.). No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class rank is published as a bar.

Applicants must have completed at least 240 ECTS education in Civil Engineering, Industrial and/or Systems Engineering, Materials Engineering, Environmental Engineering or related fields, having been awarded a recognised degree in any of such fields. For students having a study period in UNIPD (either coursework or dissertation) a minimum of 300 ECTS education is required, including specified credits in hydraulics, structural mechanics, structural engineering and geotechnics.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNIPD, 240 ECTS otherwise

requirements.text: Admission is made on a competitive basis; the students are assessed on the basis of their previous academic records. Admission is subjected to the approval of the FRP++ Managing Board and is based upon the applicant's ability and motivation, recommendation letters and language skills. Applications will be assessed solely on academic merit, ability and potential. The academic evaluation of the candidate's curriculum is based on the following criteria: previous higher education studies; content and relevance of prior studies / quality of the awarding institution; relevant professional experience; recommendation letters; motivation letter; additional information (publications, awards, etc.). No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class rank is published as a bar.

Students are expected to have a higher education degree with a minimum of: Bachelor and/or Master degree(s) with 300 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to a graduation with a total of 5 years of studies) — this requirement becomes mandatory for all students whose mobility track includes UNINA — or Bachelor degree(s) with 240 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to a graduation with a total of 4 years of studies). The degree must be in Civil Engineering, Mechanical and/or Industrial Engineering, Materials Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Polymers Engineering or related fields.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNINA, 240 ECTS otherwise

requirements.text: Ranking is performed on basis of the following criteria: academic level, University of last degree, English proficiency, motivation, reference letters. Within the eligible candidates selected, the consortium awards scholarships for mobility on basis of the score obtained in the selection ranking. No GPA, marks percentage, degree classification or numeric ranking threshold is published as a bar.

Students must have a Bachelor's Degree (180 ECTS) in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science or related disciplines: Geo-science, Nano-science, Materials engineering. (Bachelors in Mechanical engineering and in Mechatronics are not adapted to the Mamaself program.)

of.varies_by: country of study — the programme states that a minimum GPA exists and is set per country of study, but publishes no figure for any country

requirements.text: The minimum GPA (Grade Point Average) depends on the country of study, as defined by IHE Delft (based on a thorough comparative assessment done at a higher level in the Netherlands). In case of doubt, the programme coordinator is contacted. Following the eligibility check, a shortlist of around 50-80 applicants eligible for a scholarship is built by the coordinator of the programme in close collaboration with the student admission office, based on the relevance and grade of the obtained bachelor degree and followed disciplines, relevant work experience, other academic qualifications or activities, the number of applicants per country and the letter of motivation.

of.applies_to: the best 35% of students in the qualifying degree

requirements.text: The qualifying degree has to be passed with an average grade higher or equal to B (or a final grading higher or equal to B) according to the ECTS grading system, i.e. the best 35% of students (corresponding to a grade of up to 2.8 ("gut"/"good") in the German grading scale). The qualifying degree must be a first-cycle degree qualification according to the European Qualifications Framework or an equivalent degree qualification in the field of Civil Engineering, subject to an examination of equivalence by the programme's Admission Board.

This record is the European Commission's catalogue of the 218 Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes currently supported by the EU, not a programme itself, and it publishes no admission criteria. It directs applicants to "visit the program's official website and directly contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures, and scholarship availability". The academic requirement belongs to each consortium's own programme, and ScholarHub records it there — TERRA, NORISK, FRP++, MaMaSELF+, MS² and Flood Risk Management each carry their own entry in this file.

The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS) assesses scholarship applications according to three criteria: candidate profile; quality of the research project or artistic work; synergies and potential for future research cooperation. No GPA, grade average, marks percentage, class rank or credit threshold is published as a bar — the only stated prerequisites are a Master's degree and an academic supervisor in Switzerland willing to direct the proposed research. Switzerland's own 1-6 grading scale is never mentioned on the page.

No GPA, grade average, first-class average, letter grade or marks percentage is published as an eligibility requirement. Academic record appears only as one indicator inside the second of two weighted selection criteria — "Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia" (50%), whose academic-record indicators are: transcripts; duration of previous studies; program requirements and courses pursued; course load; relative standing in program (if available). The remaining 50% is research potential. The only numeric academic threshold is temporal, not grade-based: no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study by 31 December of the application year — and that is a ceiling, not a floor, so it is quoted here rather than encoded (see REQUIREMENTS-SCHEMA.md §3.5).

Selection runs on four weighted criteria — academic merit, motivation, recommendation letters, and previous experience and other skills — plus an interview, with a final score summed across them. Academic merit is scored on: Grades/GPA; "Student's ranking, if available"; and quality and ranking of the university of origin. No GPA, marks percentage or class-rank threshold is published as a bar. The page also states that places without scholarships go to applicants "whose ranking exceeds a minimum eligibility threshold", and does not publish that threshold — the same shape as Flood Risk Management: a bar that exists and is not stated. NOTE ON WHAT COULD NOT BE READ: this page's "Academic requirements" block (degree and credit prerequisites) renders as a collapsed accordion and was not readable, so no credit or degree figure is claimed for this record in either direction — its absence here is not a finding that none exists.

Selection is carried out as a cooperative process between the academic partner universities, with the final selection based on consensus, and is "based on academic qualifications, with a focus on qualitative and quantitative indicators of the applicants": academic background; motivation letter and video; language skills; work experience. Applicants are rated and the 40 highest-rated are invited to interview. No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class-rank threshold is published as a bar.

Candidates must have a Bachelor's degree in Engineering with basic knowledge in Geology (minimum 3 years of study or 180 ECTS credits), or a Bachelor's degree in Minerals Engineering, Mining Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Geological Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, or Materials Engineering (if oriented towards metals extraction and processing), or a Master's degree in Geology.
The EMerald Master Programme provides an engineering diploma, therefore at least 22.5 ECTS in university level mathematics is required for application eligibility.

BIOPHAM publishes no GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class-rank threshold, and no ranked list of selection criteria. What it does publish is that academic preparation is judged on subject background: "all applicants from eligible fields should possess sufficient background in physics and mathematics related topics usually a minimum 18 ECTS each during the Bachelor studies. This background will be assessed by the Selection Committee during the selection procedure." It also restricts eligible fields to five (Physics, Materials Science, Chemistry, Nanoscience, Bioengineering) and publishes an explicit list of fields it will not consider.
Applicants should hold, or be in the process of obtaining, a first higher education degree in science (e.g., Bachelor, Licence, or equivalent to 180 credits or 180 ECTS) at the time of application.

of.applies_to: physics and mathematics — 18 ECTS in each

requirements.text: All applicants from eligible fields should possess sufficient background in physics and mathematics related topics usually a minimum 18 ECTS each during the Bachelor studies. This background will be assessed by the Selection Committee during the selection procedure.
requirements.not_a_requirement: BIOPHAM words this as "should possess ... usually a minimum" and says the background "will be assessed by the Selection Committee", not that it is an eligibility gate. It is an expectation weighed in selection, and is recorded separately from the 180-ECTS degree requirement precisely so the two are not read as the same kind of bar.

requirements.text: The scholarship itself publishes no academic threshold whatsoever. Its eligibility criteria are: foreign nationality; admission to a master's degree at Universite Paris-Saclay; first-time enrolment in France; under 30 during the year of application; and no other funding above 600 EUR per month. The jury evaluates "academic background, personal project, motivation for pursuing a PhD thesis at Universite Paris-Saclay (M2 candidates)", and the page states plainly that "the jury being discretionary, its decisions are confidential and cannot lead to appeal". Any academic bar therefore lives in the master's programme's own admission decision, not here — the same delegated bar as Chevening, whose 2:1 is set by the university's unconditional offer rather than by the scholarship.

The NL Scholarship (formerly the Holland Scholarship) publishes no academic threshold of its own. Its application criteria are: nationality outside the EEA; applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution; not already holding a degree from an institution in the Netherlands; and, in the programme's own words, "You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice. You can find these on the website of the institution." The academic bar is therefore set separately by each of the 34 participating research universities and universities of applied sciences, and the central page publishes none of them. The award is EUR 5,000 for the first year and is explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship.

MSCA Doctoral Networks publish no academic threshold, and this is structural rather than an omission: the funding goes to consortia, and each beneficiary recruits its own doctoral candidates. "Candidates wishing to apply for PhD positions under Doctoral Networks should apply to funded Doctoral Network projects by consulting their open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal", and EURAXESS is where the full requirements of a given position live. The individual eligibility conditions the central page does state are not academic: researchers "must not have a doctoral degree at the date of their recruitment", "can be of any nationality", "should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project", and must satisfy the mobility rule — "they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date". Note also that these are salaried positions rather than scholarships.

Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships publish no academic threshold of their own, and say so explicitly: "Successful scholarship applicants must meet both the academic entry requirements and the English language requirements determined by the applicant's preferred education institutions", and "Each university or education institution sets the minimum level of English required, so check their websites for information." The programme's own eligibility criteria are non-academic but strict: citizenship of an eligible country; residence in the home country for the two years before applying; at least 18 years old at signing the offer ("There is no upper age limit for applicants. However, we do prefer applicants who are under 40 years of age"); for postgraduate applicants, relevant work experience of one year full-time or two years part-time; and no disqualifying previous Manaaki award. It publishes indicative English levels as a guide only — for postgraduate study, generally IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 90 with a writing score of 21 — and states "The information above is a guide only. Some courses have higher minimum English level entry requirements than those outlined."

No GPA, grade average, marks percentage, degree classification or class-rank threshold is published. The academic bar is delegated: "Eligible applicants should meet the admission criteria for international students of USTC/UCAS" — the two host universities — and the scholarship page does not restate them. Its own eligibility criteria are citizenship, nationality on the TWAS developing-country list, proficiency in English or Chinese, and age: "For PhD program applicants: you should be born after 1st January 1991 (inclusive)", with the page's structured age-limit field reading 35. The minimum degree held is an MSc, and the level is PhD. Up to 40 PhD students are selected each year from developing countries, 10 of them prioritised for climate-related research, with special (non-exclusive) consideration for Least Developed Countries and for women. The page publishes no scoring rubric for the application stage; the qualification test it mentions is a post-award condition, not an entry requirement.

PARTIAL — read only at the programme level. This page publishes no academic eligibility criterion at all: it describes the award's benefits and conditions, and links out to "Country information" covering participating countries and opening and closing dates. The country-level application pages, which are where eligibility is expected to be set, were not read — one fetch of the "how to apply" page timed out. So no credit or degree figure is claimed here in either direction, and the absence of an academic threshold on this record is NOT a finding that the programme has none.

JJ/WBGSP publishes no GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class-rank threshold. It publishes something rarer: the weights of its scoring rubric. Two assessors independently score each eligible application out of 10 on four factors — quality of professional experience (30%), quality of professional recommendations (30%), quality of commitment to the home country (30%), and quality of education background (10%). Academic record is therefore the smallest of four components, and a reader optimising for this award should not optimise for grades. The eligibility gates are non-academic and hard: nationality of a World Bank member developing country, no dual citizenship of a developed country, a bachelor's degree earned at least 3 years before the deadline, at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past 6 years, and unconditional admission (except for funding) to one of the 44 participating master's programmes. "All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to. No exceptions are made."

The Pan African University states a real academic bar, and it is a degree classification rather than a number: master's applicants must be a "Holder of an Undergraduate degree from a recognised university, with at least a second-class upper division or its equivalent, in a relevant field", and "Academic Competence must be evidenced in academic transcripts at the bachelors' level." The equivalent for a non-UK transcript is left to the university to judge — the provider supplies no conversion — which is why this is recorded as prose and not as a figure. The other requirements are non-academic and unusually specific: age limits of not older than 25 for male and 28 for female master's applicants, and 28 male / 30 female for doctoral applicants, plus a written or oral examination after pre-selection. Doctoral applicants need a master's degree in a relevant field and a 3 to 4 page research concept note.

The Humphrey Fellowship publishes no academic threshold at all, and this is a statement about the programme rather than a gap in the record: it is a non-degree fellowship for mid-career professionals, and selection is "based on excellence in professional and personal qualifications as well as leadership potential". The gate is professional experience — at least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in Nepal by the deadline, at mid-career policy level, with volunteer work, internships and work done for an academic degree explicitly excluded. The one degree-shaped rule is structural rather than graded: professional experience must follow "a 4-year bachelor's degree, or, if the bachelor's degree is of 2-year/3-year duration, then a master's degree is also required", and candidates holding two or more short bachelor's degrees without a master's are not eligible. The competition is also closed to recent graduates, to university teachers without management or policy responsibility, and to anyone with substantial recent U.S. experience.

REM+ 2 states that its admission criteria are not yet published, which is a finding rather than an absence. The whole of its admission page reads: "The selection and admission procedure for this EMJM is currently under review by the Joint Programme Board (JPB). The updated procedure will be published on this website shortly. Thank you for your understanding." (last update 16 September 2026). No GPA, marks, ECTS, degree-field or English threshold is published anywhere on the page. A reader should check back rather than assume the programme is unselective — and note that this is deliberately NOT recorded as `unstated`: the provider states something definite about the state of its own procedure, and that statement belongs in the record.

TFMASA publishes no GPA, marks percentage, class-rank or degree-classification threshold. Its standard is stated qualitatively and repeatedly — "a strong academic record and a solid foundation in engineering sciences, applied physics, mathematics, and mechanics are essential", "A strong academic profile is expected, as TFMASA is a highly selective programme" — and the only quantitative academic requirement is the credit load. Note what it asks to be ranked: the CV "must clearly" show the ranking of the University or Engineering School, which is the institution's standing rather than the applicant's class rank — the same substitution KTH makes.
Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree (or equivalent, 180 ECTS) in Mechanics, Physics, or a closely related field before the start of the programme.

IELTS (Academic Test): 6.5 with no score below 6; TOEFL paper-based 580, computer-based 237, internet-based 93; Certificate of Advanced English: B/C; Certificate of Proficiency in English: B/C; or a letter from the applicant's university stating that the medium of instruction was English. Exemptions may apply for native English speakers or those who completed prior education in English. The test must have been completed no more than 3 years before the course starts, and Primary and Secondary Education certificates or 1-year exchange programme documentation are accepted as English certificates.
